title: Consolidated ingress: compact KV trace enrichment and multi-source merging
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Multiple ingress adapters (kafka-shaper, edge-gateway, telemetry preprocessor) are emitting overlapping structured log formats and duplicate trace metadata. This causes high cardinality tag explosion in Loki indexes, inconsistent correlation-id propagation for chained RPCs, and increased tokenization/costs in downstream pipelines.

Goal: Build a consolidated ingress stage that performs compact KV-style trace enrichment, deterministic multi-source merging, and tenant-aware low-cardinality normalization before logs hit Kafka and Loki. The stage must preserve original event fidelity, support dynamic schema adapters, and run with bounded CPU/memory on the existing ingest fleet.

Constraints: Must be backward compatible with current log producers for 3 months, introduce no more than 10ms median per-event processing overhead at 99th percentile in steady state, and operate without external coordination during autoscaling events. The implementation should prefer deterministic, idempotent transforms (i.e., canonicalize trace IDs, collapse repeated KV pairs into compact arrays) and expose feature flags for gradual rollout per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress stage is deployed behind a feature flag and can be toggled per-tenant via Console
Correlation IDs are normalized to canonical 64-bit hex for all incoming trace headers and linked across multi-hop spans
Cardinality for tenant+service+error_type tags reduces by at least 40% in Loki index sample compared to baseline
No dropped mandatory fields (timestamp, message, tenant_id, trace_id) during merge for 99.99% of events
Benchmark: median per-event CPU < 6ms and p99 < 12ms on ingest node under 80% load
End-to-end tests and fuzzer added covering mixed schema inputs (JSON, ndjson, protobuf)
tasks: Draft transformation spec for canonical trace id format and KV compaction rules
Prototype a Go-based ingestion worker with pluggable adapters for JSON/ndjson/protobuf
Integrate deterministic merge logic to reconcile fields from multiple sources (producer priority rules)
Add tenant-aware low-cardinality mapping table with TTL and eviction policy
Wire feature-flag toggle and per-tenant rollout hooks in control-plane API
Create regression suite and load benchmark harness using k6 + local Loki instance
Document schema changes and update Console toggle UI path
progress_updates: 2025-11-10: Initial spec reviewed with Observability and Platform SREs. Agreed on canonical 64-bit hex trace_id and producer priority ordering: agent > edge > aggregator.
2025-12-02: Prototype ingest worker implemented; JSON and ndjson adapters functional. Early benchmark shows median 3.8ms, p99 14ms (p99 needs optimization).
2026-01-15: Introduced compact-KV encoder that collapses repeated keys into arrays and strips nulls; reduced sample index cardinality ~28% in synthetic tenant test.
2026-02-22: Hooked module into Kafka ingress path and validated end-to-end pipeline on staging with two tenants. Observed increased GC pause at high concurrency—investigating buffer pool reuse.
2026-03-03: Added tenant mapping with LRU eviction; updated merge rules to preserve top-level message field deterministically. Preparing rollout plan for 10 internal tenants.
comments: Maya Chen (Observability): Please ensure the canonicalization preserves upstream trace variants like X-Request-ID fallback. We rely on that for legacy services.
Daniel Park (SRE): The LRU eviction must be bounded and transparent in metrics; add per-tenant eviction rate and missed-lookups gauge.
Design Review (Ana Rodriguez): Compacting repeated KV into arrays is good, but we need to keep an example mapping table in the docs so users can interpret arrays in logs.
Lucas Ortega: Will follow up with a memory profiling session to eliminate the GC spikes; considering sync.Pool and preallocated byte buffers.
